title: TikTok's For You Page: free virality for the behavioral graph
summary: The For You Page is the most generous distribution machine ever built: an interest graph, not a social graph, so a video from an account with zero followers can reach millions if it clears each engagement gate. The price of that generosity is the complete behavioral graph — watch time, completions, replays, pauses, likes, comments, shares, follows — used to train a ranking model the user can never inspect, tune, or take with them.
mechanism: Interest-graph cascade: each video is tested against small pools of viewers matched by topic signals; clearing the engagement gate widens distribution to larger pools. TikTok's own transparency page lists the inputs: region, language, device OS, videos watched/finished/liked/skipped, follow relationships; the model predicts likelihood to like, share, comment, finish, skip, favorite, time spent, and soundtrack taps. The strongest signal is completion — finishing a video outweighs a like. TikTok's own 2020 guidance: 'the best way to curate your For You feed is to simply use and enjoy the app' — i.e., surrender implicit signals, not declare explicit preferences. In December 2022 TikTok added a 'Why this video' panel (share menu), which names coarse categories ('you liked similar videos', 'popular in your region') but discloses no weights and offers no per-signal control.
decline: Not dead — dominant. The honest version of this pattern (declared rationale + user-controlled ranking weights) has never shipped at scale because opacity IS the product: a legible, tunable feed would let users optimize for their own goals instead of the platform's retention metric, and the behavioral training data is the moat.
revival_recipe: Build the feed TikTok refuses: every recommendation ships with a machine-checkable rationale record (which signals fired, at what declared weight), all weights user-tunable, and a visible 'why am I seeing this' ledger that is the primary UI rather than a buried share-menu afterthought.
levi_application: LEVI's recommender already scores with declared weights and explanations (core/levi/recommender, core/levi/feedlab: 'the contributions ARE the explanation'). The addition this hunt ships is the counter-catalog entry plus a portable Flow Declaration (core/levi/fairtrade/flows.py): any feed-like surface LEVI builds must declare its data flows — signals collected, purpose, retention, user control — with the declarant's own collection subject to the same rules.
skepticism: Cascade pool sizes (300-500 initial viewers) and 2025-26 'qualified view' threshold changes come from third-party marketing writeups, not TikTok; treated as reported, not verified. 'Why this video' granularity described from TechCrunch's 2022 launch coverage; current behavior may differ.

title: Discord: free community infrastructure with no exit
summary: Discord gives communities unlimited free voice, text, and video infrastructure — the most generous community-hosting offer on the internet. The capture: a community cannot leave. Discord's 'Request My Data' export covers only messages sent by the requesting user; received messages from other members are excluded, attachment CDN URLs expire, and there is no first-party community migration path — no portable server archive (structure, roles, full history, member graph) that another platform or a self-hosted tool can import.
mechanism: The generosity is individual and the lock-in is collective. Each member gets a personal data package (their own sent messages only), but the community — the thing with value — has no export artifact. Meanwhile basic community features are paywalled behind Nitro ($9.99/mo) and Server Boosts (vanity URL, upload limits, emoji slots, HD voice). The community's history, culture, and social graph live on Discord's servers under Discord's terms; a ban or a terms change strands the community with nowhere to go and nothing to take.
decline: Not dead — 150M+ monthly users. The pattern persists because coordination cost is the moat: even members who know they are tenants cannot coordinate an exit without the very infrastructure they would be leaving. Third-party tools (bots, data-package browsers) fill the gap partially, which lets Discord keep the official export individual-only without regulatory pressure.
revival_recipe: Ship the community escrow LEVI's games module already proves for games (sunset.py: offline patch, content export, state export): a community manifest declaring exactly what a community owns and can take — member roster, message history, media, roles/permissions, bot/webhook configs — plus a drill that verifies the export against real artifacts. Export must be community-portable, not just individual-portable.
levi_application: Seeded as a Discord ServiceProfile in core/levi/liberation (hostage scoring now covers the community-graph variant), and cataloged as the 'community-graph-hostage' sly-trade pattern in core/levi/fairtrade/trades.py with its counterplay: LEVI communities (circles, hives) export whole — one command, everything, import-grade — because the gift must survive the user leaving with all of it.
skepticism: Export limitations described from third-party tooling documentation (Memoria, skills4sh), not Discord's own support pages; Discord may have changed package contents since. Nitro/Boost pricing from public knowledge; not re-verified this run.

title: GitHub Copilot: free tools in, training data out, protection sold back
summary: GitHub gave developers free world-class tools — free repos, free VS Code, free Actions minutes — and trained Copilot (technical preview June 2021, GA June 2022 at $10/mo) on the public code those tools attracted, including open-source-licensed code. In November 2022 anonymous developers filed a class action (Doe v. GitHub/Microsoft/OpenAI) alleging training on OSS code without license compliance; by June 2024 most claims were dismissed but breach-of-contract claims proceeded. The sly trade: the exclusion controls (keep my code out of training/suggestions) are organization/admin controls on paid tiers — protection from the toll is sold back to the people who paid it.
mechanism: Two-sided funnel. Side one: free, excellent tools with telemetry on by default attract the code. Side two: the code trains a $10/mo ($19/user/mo enterprise) product sold back to the same developers. The contributor has no after-the-fact opt-out, no standing in the training decision, and no share of the revenue. GitHub's stated position: training on public code is fair use — a legal theory the November 2022 suit called 'pure speculation' and courts have not fully settled.
decline: Not dead — the industry standard now. The pattern persists because each individual developer's rational move (use the free tool, ship faster) is collectively self-taxing, and no single contributor can negotiate terms with the platform that hosts the commons.
revival_recipe: The inversion is provenance-by-default plus a machine-checkable training-consent declaration: every artifact LEVI trains on carries a consent record (who agreed, scope, revocability), and LEVI's own brain is trained on its own corpus — never on user data without explicit, revocable, per-artifact consent. Consent must be free-tier and individual, never a paid-tier admin control.
levi_application: Cataloged as the 'training-data-toll' sly-trade pattern in core/levi/fairtrade/trades.py with counterplay: LEVI's native brain trains on LEVI's own corpus (local-first, stdlib-only); growth writes only growth-tagged local memory; provenance module tracks artifact origins. This hunt adds the portable Flow Declaration (core/levi/fairtrade/flows.py) so any LEVI training flow must declare data, purpose, retention, and user control — the declaration the giants refuse to make.
skepticism: Content-exclusion being a paid-tier admin control is per GitHub's public docs as widely reported; not re-verified against current docs this run. VS Code telemetry default is documented default behavior; not re-verified this run. Legal status summarized from Wikipedia; not legal advice.
